label: digit 0 fed back as input during the copy phase (from the 4th output on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the token fed back as input is the digit 0 (so the original 0 sat at position >= 2) and the step outputs original token 3 or later. In the original phase and at the delimiter it never fires, even when 0 is the input. It is silent on every other input token (only a few dozen stray hits). Magnitude grows with how far into the copy the 0 is: a 0 copied back at original position 2 gives weak activations (about 0.1-0.4 of max, mostly below the predicate threshold), and 0s later in the sequence reach about 0.5-1.0 of max. The top examples often have h just before the 0, but prev_tok lift is weak (1.3x), so that is not a reliable modulator. Rate per eligible step rises with the number of digits in the sequence only because more digits means more 0s.

issues: Main claims hold on test. Predicate: P 0.995, R 0.965, F1 0.980, mass recall 0.994. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase: '(in_tok==0)&(phase!=2)' fires on 0 of 108,710 steps. Copy-phase steps with non-0 inputs: 0.28% recall, 0.02% of mass, so the stray hits are scattered noise.

Misses (2,084 steps, 0.6% of mass) are weak copy-phase 0s at recall_idx 2, plus a few at recall_idx 1 in L=3 sequences (for example 'h 0 3 <DEL> h [0:0.27]'). Most are 0.03-0.3 of max. That matches the stated weak activations at recall_idx 2. The recall_idx==2 slice alone has precision 0.11, so it is correctly left out.

False positives are 273 steps (about 0.5%), and some cluster at recall_idx 3, where the 0 being fed back was original position 2 (for example L=7, t=10). This is small and does not change the verdict.

Minor wording issue: recall_idx >= 3 means the 0 being fed back is the 3rd original token or later, and the step outputs the 4th original token or later. '(from the 4th output on)' can be misread as 'the 0 is the 4th output'. The explanation text states it correctly.
